questions.note: In the onion the head size, skull top, shoulder line, elbow heights and foot spread land close to the reference. The upper arms and shoulders read a little thicker than drawn, because the sleeves are full and the right shoulder plate stands proud. The legs differ as declared. Nothing reads as a different man's frame.

The stance, foot splay, arm angles and the carbine's diagonal match the reference well in the onion. Departures: the head is turned only about 10 degrees to his left with the chin level (the reference is about 25 degrees with the chin raised); the right shoulder plate pokes up above the drawn shoulder line; the right boot's long flat toe changes the foot outline.

Every item is present and roughly where drawn, but several are the wrong form or sit in the wrong place: the right pauldron perches on top of the shoulder; light bands ring the upper arms where the reference has plates; the right forearm guard is an elbow cuff; the right leg rig sits on the front of the thigh as twin boxes; the knee pads are about 20% too wide; the antenna is black.

The order is right (shirt, trousers, boots, gloves, carrier, belt, armour, carbine), and I saw no clear interpenetration in the hero frame. But the right shoulder plate lifts off the arm with a gap, an L-shaped belt item at the right rear hip juts out into the air, and the radio pouch hangs beyond the back plate's edge with nothing visibly holding it.

The build is close. But the carrier reads as a thin, plain slab with short pouches instead of the reference's loaded front, the knee pads are oversized, the sleeves balloon around the upper arms, and the trousers cling at the seat yet balloon at the shins. The kit reads less loaded and heavy than the reference's, and softer.

The carbine's line, the stock along the right forearm, and the right hand on the grip with the index finger along the receiver all match. The left hand differs: it clamps the handguard overhand from above, about 80 px back toward the magwell. In the reference it is further forward and cradles the handguard, with the fingers curling up from below on the near side.

defects.what: The head is turned only about 10 degrees to the soldier's left with the chin level. The reference's head is turned about 25 degrees to his left, the chin slightly raised, the gaze off to the viewer's right.
defects.fix: Turn the head further to his left and lift the chin a few degrees, as in the reference.

defects.what: The hair is a smooth, dark, helmet-like cap with a hard straight hairline across the forehead. The reference has a short textured brown crop with a lifted front, receding temples and visible strands.
defects.fix: Give the hair a groomed short crop: volume at the front, a soft broken hairline, and the reference's brown.

defects.what: The right shoulder plate is a flat slab sitting on top of the shoulder beside the collar. It stands proud of the arm with a gap and rises about 50 px above the reference's curved shell, which sits on the outer deltoid.
defects.fix: Curve the plate to the deltoid and hang it lower on the outer shoulder, strapped flush to the sleeve.

defects.what: Pale grey bands ring both upper arms and read as the brightest stripes on the figure. In the reference the upper arms carry darker plates on their outer faces, with only a dark strap under the left pauldron.
defects.fix: Replace the rings with outer upper-arm plates on dark webbing straps, valued like the rest of the armour.

defects.what: The carrier front is a plain plate bag with a soft flap and four short open-top pouches. It lacks the reference's admin panel, the vertical shoulder-strap webbing and buckles down each side of the chest, and the three tall flapped mag pouches.
defects.fix: Build the reference's front: an admin panel up top, strap runs and buckles at each side, and a placard of three tall flapped pouches.

defects.what: The carrier and pouches are a flat grey-khaki with little value range. The reference's are a warmer coyote-olive with dark grime in the recesses and pale scuffed edges.
defects.fix: Shift the base toward coyote-olive, and add grime in the recesses and abrasion on the edges and the pouch flaps.

defects.what: The pauldrons, arm bands, and elbow and forearm guards are all a uniform pale warm grey, clean and plastic-looking. The reference's armour is a darker gunmetal grey-olive with heavy scratches, dark grime and tan-gold edge wear.
defects.fix: Darken the armour base and add scratched edges, grime in the seams and worn tan edges, as drawn.

defects.what: The left pauldron is a flat plate with a pale square patch below it and a band round the arm. The reference's pauldron is a domed shell over the deltoid, with a second plate and a buckle tab on the outer upper arm.
defects.fix: Dome the shoulder shell and add the second outer-arm plate with its buckle tab.

defects.what: The right forearm guard is a short smooth cylinder plus an elbow cup, both at the elbow. The reference's guard covers the forearm from the elbow to the wrist, in segments with straps.
defects.fix: Lengthen the guard down the forearm to the glove cuff and split it into strapped segments.

defects.what: The left forearm guard is a smooth flared cone, wider than the reference's and sitting nearer the elbow. The reference's guard is segmented and strapped, and closer to the wrist.
defects.fix: Narrow it to the forearm, move it toward the wrist, and add segment breaks and a strap.

defects.what: The right leg rig is two identical square black boxes with tan face plates, side by side on the front of the thigh. The reference has a single, narrower drop-leg platform (holster and mag pouch) on the outer side of the thigh, on two straps.
defects.fix: Use one narrow drop-leg platform on the outer thigh, with its two thigh straps visible.

defects.what: The knee pads are soft, pillow-shaped shells about 20% wider than drawn, with no hard faceted cap. The reference's pads have a hexagonal hard cap with a raised tan rim over a padded base.
defects.fix: Narrow the pads to the drawn width and model the faceted hard cap with its tan rim on a softer base.

defects.what: The right boot's lower is a smooth moulded shell, like a galosh, with a long flat toe, and its lacing stops at the top of the instep. The reference's boot is lace-to-toe leather, with a rounded toe cap, a rand and stitched panels.
defects.fix: Run the eyelets down to the toe box, round the toe cap, and add a rand and panelling as on the left boot and the reference.

defects.what: The trouser legs don't match: the right leg is near-black, while the left shin has large, contrasty cloud-camo blotches. In the reference both legs share an even, dusty grey-brown mottle with lighter dust low on the shins.
defects.fix: Use one camo scale and contrast on both legs, with dust building toward the hems.

defects.what: An L-shaped item at the right rear hip juts out horizontally from the belt, standing off the body (also visible in the back and left-side turnarounds).
defects.fix: Seat it on the belt so it hangs vertically and flush against the hip.

defects.what: The radio pouch hangs beyond the back plate's left edge, with nothing visible attaching it to the carrier.
defects.fix: Mount it on the back panel's PALS or the cummerbund so it rests on the carrier.

defects.what: The antenna is black with a rounded ball tip. In the reference it is a tan-brass tube with a yellow end.
defects.fix: Match the reference's tan tube and yellow tip.

defects.what: The left hand clamps the handguard overhand from above, about 80 px back toward the magwell. In the reference it sits further forward and cradles the handguard, the fingers curling up from below on the near side.
defects.fix: Slide the hand forward along the handguard and rotate it to support from beneath.

defects.what: The trouser seat clings to the buttocks like leggings, while below the knee the legs balloon. A G3-class trouser is roomy at the seat and the thigh and tapers toward the ankle.
defects.fix: Give the seat and thighs ease and cut the lower legs fuller only where the blousing gathers.

ranked: [D7] The armour is uniformly pale, clean grey, so it reads as plastic. The reference's plates are darker gunmetal-olive, heavily scratched and grimed, with tan edge wear. This is the biggest giveaway at native size.
[D4] The pale bands around both upper arms are the brightest marks on the figure and draw the eye; the reference has dark plates and straps there.
[D5] The carrier front is too plain: no admin panel, none of the strap webbing and buckles down each side, and short open pouches instead of three tall flapped ones.
[D6] The carrier is a grey-khaki with little value range, against the reference's warm coyote-olive with grime and scuffs.
[D12] The knee pads are oversized soft pillows. The reference's pads are faceted hard caps with a tan rim, narrower.
[D13] The right boot's lower is a smooth galosh with a long flat toe and no lacing over the instep; the reference wears lace-to-toe leather boots.
[D3] The right shoulder plate perches flat on top of the shoulder by the collar and stands off the arm. The reference's is a curved shell low on the deltoid.
[D1] The head is turned too little toward his left and the chin is level, which loses the reference's alert, off-camera gaze.
[D2] The hair is a smooth dark cap with a hard hairline, not the reference's textured, lifted brown crop.
[D11] The right leg rig is twin square boxes on the front of the thigh instead of a single narrow drop-leg platform on the outer thigh.
[D14] The trouser legs don't match each other: one leg is near-black, the other has big contrasty camo blotches. The reference is an even dusty mottle on both legs.
[D9] The right forearm guard is an elbow cuff; the reference's runs down the forearm to the wrist in strapped segments.
[D18] The left hand grips the handguard overhand and too far back, instead of cradling it from below further forward.
[D8] The left pauldron is a flat plate plus a band; the reference has a domed shell and a second outer-arm plate.
There is no grime, dust or edge wear anywhere on the kit, so the whole figure reads newer, cleaner and lower in contrast than the battle-worn reference.
The sleeves balloon around the upper arms, which makes the arms read thicker and softer than the reference's fitted combat shirt under armour.
[D10] The left forearm guard is a smooth, oversized cone near the elbow, not a segmented guard near the wrist.
[D19] The trouser seat clings like leggings while the shins balloon; the cut is inverted against a G3-class trouser.
[D15] An L-shaped belt item at the right rear hip juts straight out from the body in the turnarounds.
[D17] The antenna is black with a ball tip; the reference's is a tan tube with a yellow end.
[D16] The radio pouch hangs off the back plate's edge, attached to nothing visible.
